KEY MESSAGE 1...Periods of rain showers will impact the area
through much of the day, and lingering into tonight for Delmarva
and far southern New Jersey.

Massive High pressure well to the north is beginning to push its
influence southward across the southern Poconos and north NJ
early this afternoon. Clouds are thinning as a North to Northeast
flow strengthens. The north edge of the steady rains (currently
across Delmarva and south NJ) continues to slowly push 
southward. These showers will continue early tonight before 
ending. Wednesday should be a fair weather day and with the 
drier air deepening across the region More widespread sunshine 
is expected, but still some cloudiness for Delmarva and 
southern-most NJ. 

A continuing Northeast flow tonight and Wednesday will result in 
more below normal temperatures with highs struggling to get out
of the 60s areawide Wed. and the rest of the week. Lows will 
range from the mid 40s to 50s this week.


KEY MESSAGE 2...A strengthening surface low off the Eastern 
Seaboard during the middle and latter parts of this week will 
keep persistent northeast to north flow in place through at 
least Friday. Depending on the track of the low, it could bring 
increased rainfall chances and windy conditions to the parts of 
the region Friday and into the weekend.

A mid-level impulse currently traversing portions of the 
Midwest into the Ohio Valley will continue eastward towards the 
Eastern Seaboard tonight into Wednesday. Weak surface 
cyclogenesis has begun off the coast of the Carolinas, with the 
low expected to continue intensifying through late this week. 
The initial track of the developing low is expected to be to the
northeast, well offshore. However, with a strong high centered 
over portions of Quebec, a sharp pressure gradient over the 
region will at least lead to breezy conditions beginning today 
through Thursday near the coast. The strongest pressure 
gradient, and thus winds, are forecast to occur on Wednesday 
into Wednesday night. It should remain mostly dry during the 
Wednesday through Thursday period, though some showers may 
linger across Delmarva Wednesday morning.

Given a consistent forecast for sustained winds 25-35 mph along
the Atlantic coasts of New Jersey and Delaware on Wednesday, a 
Wind Advisory will be in effect for the immediate coastal strip 
from 6 AM Wednesday through midnight Wednesday night. Some gusts
near 45 mph are also possible.

For late this week into this weekend, model guidance remains 
largely split into two camps. One camp allows the low to 
continue to track northeastward away from the region, and the 
other camp features a westward deviation of the low, or even 
additional surface cyclogenesis closer to the coast. Given these
factors, uncertainty for Friday and beyond remains quite high, 
with a large range of potential outcomes. The deterministic EC 
and all of its ensembles continue to feature the scenario that 
would lead to greater impacts. The deterministic GFS remains far
enough out to sea to keep impacts confined to the immediate 
coast with gusty winds and minimal rainfall. However, it should 
be noted that the GFS has trended westward somewhat this 
afternoon, and a few GEFS members feature solutions fairly 
similar to the EC. It is unclear whether this is a single-run 
deviation or the beginning of the development of better model 
consensus. For now feature PoPs in the 20-40% range along the 
coast Friday, expanding inland to the I-95 corridor Saturday and
areawide Saturday night into Sunday. Regardless of which 
scenario pans out, precipitation chances and winds will be 
highest close to the coast and decrease with inland extent. 

Sunday night into Monday, regardless of which scenario 
ultimately pans out, the low will begin to track away from the 
area, allowing rain chances to decrease and winds to subside.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Multiple rounds of potentially significant 
tidal flooding expected for this week. The first batch of 
Coastal Flood headlines remain in effect with more likely to 
come.

With a slow moving coastal storm increasingly likely, the 
threat for tidal flooding has increased. Strong onshore flow 
that is projected to last for several days will result in water 
piling up across tidal tributaries and within back bays of 
coastal communities. Tidal levels will also be enhanced with 
astronomical tides increasing with the upcoming Full Moon on 
Saturday. This combination of factors will lead to widespread 
tidal flooding, some of which could get to the Moderate stage. 
While not currently forecast, the threat for major flooding is 
not off the table, especially getting near the full moon. 

Minor tidal flooding begins as early as tomorrow afternoon and 
evening for some locations. A Coastal Flood Advisory was issued 
for Ocean, Atlantic, and Cape May County in New Jersey and Kent
